question: In the channelized-intersection example in Figure 2A-3, how far from the nose of the island is the YIELD sign shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B ("Channelized intersection") of Figure 2A-3, the YIELD sign for the channelized right-turn roadway is shown with a lateral offset of "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." from the nose (edge) of the channelizing island. Per the figure's note, the 6-foot minimum is measured from the edge of the shoulder and the 12-foot minimum from the edge of the traveled way. (By contrast, the sign placed on the triangular island itself is dimensioned with a 2 ft MIN. clearance from the island edges.) Guidance (recommended): - "Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16." (This corresponds to the 2 ft MIN. dimension shown for the sign on the island in Drawing B; the YIELD sign beside the turn roadway is instead dimensioned at 6 ft to 12 ft MIN.) Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-3, Drawing B shows the YIELD sign positioned with "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." offset from the island nose/edge of the channelized turn roadway, while the sign on the triangular island shows "2 ft MIN." clearances; the note explains that the lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. - [Image 4] (Page 52 full-page view of Figure 2A-3) confirms the same "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." dimension pointing to the YIELD sign in Drawing B and the 2 ft MIN. dimensions for the island-mounted sign. Citations: - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Page 93 - Section 8A.06 Guidance §3 (p.989)
gold_answer: At least 2 feet from the nose of the island.
